context: mechanical-led · deep wet/dry wells · pump & wet commissioning

brief.intro: A pumping station lifts water, wastewater or stormwater from a low level up to a higher one or into a pressurised main. It is a compact but mechanical- and electrical-intensive civil structure — a wet well where flow collects, a dry well or valve chamber housing the pumps, and a switchroom of controls. New to this type? The hard part is not the building: it is the deep, watertight substructure (often below the water table) and getting the pumps, pipework and controls proven under real flow. The programme is driven by the excavation and structure first, then pump procurement and wet commissioning.

scope.name: Site enabling & dewatering
scope.desc: Access, diversions, excavation support (shoring/sheet piles) and dewatering of a deep, often below-water-table dig.

scope.name: Wet well / sump structure
scope.desc: Watertight reinforced-concrete sump where incoming flow collects; benching and inlet works.

scope.name: Dry well / pump chamber
scope.desc: Chamber or valve house holding the pumps, pipework and access.

scope.name: Pumps & pipework
scope.desc: Duty/standby pumps, suction and delivery pipework, penstocks and non-return valves.

scope.name: Valves & surge protection
scope.desc: Isolation and control valves, air valves, and surge/water-hammer protection on the rising main.

scope.name: Electrical & MCC
scope.desc: Motor control centre, variable-frequency drives, standby generator and cabling.

scope.name: Controls, SCADA & telemetry
scope.desc: Level sensors, instrumentation, PLC/SCADA and remote telemetry to the operations centre.

scope.name: Odour control & ventilation
scope.desc: For wastewater stations — odour-control units and forced ventilation of the wet well.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Dry checks, then wet commissioning and a performance / duty-standby changeover test under real flow.

glossary.plain: the underground sump where incoming flow collects before it is pumped.
the chamber that houses the pumps and pipework, kept dry.
one pump runs (duty) while another waits as backup (standby) so flow never stops.
variable-frequency drive — electronics that vary a pump's speed to match the flow.
the pressurised pipe the station pumps into.
a pressure shock when a pump trips; surge vessels protect the main.
net positive suction head — enough suction pressure so the pump doesn't cavitate.
remote monitoring and control of the station from an operations centre.

must_get_right: Deep excavation and dewatering drive the early programme — get the structure watertight before any M&E goes in.
Pumps, VFDs and switchgear are long-lead — order them before the structure is finished.
Leave real time for wet commissioning and the duty/standby performance test — it needs live flow to prove.
A live-flow tie-in (into an operating network) needs a planned outage and over-pumping — coordinate it early.

components.name: Civil structure (wet/dry well)
components.desc: Deep watertight RC sump & pump chamber

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network in Primavera P6 developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress; calculated by F9 with total float kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil works on a 6-day week; dewatering runs continuously (24/7) once started; wet commissioning uses a 7-day calendar to work around live-flow windows. Weather / groundwater allowance held in the excavation phase.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs dewatering → excavation support → wet-well structure → watertightness → pump & pipework install → electrical energisation → wet commissioning → performance test. The structure, not the M&E, governs the front; commissioning under live flow governs the tail.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Dewatering discharge consents and a stable draw-down are in place; the water table and ground are as per the GI; a single mobilisation; and any tie-in outage into the live network is granted when required.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is procurement-led on the mechanical and electrical plant — tracked as milestones:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Deep confined-space working, restricted crane access over a small footprint, and a live-flow tie-in that needs over-pumping and a planned outage are the main constraints.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: groundwater / dewatering under-performance, long-lead pump slippage, and the live tie-in window. Contingency is held before the watertightness test and before wet commissioning.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1–2 to the client, controlled at Level 3, expanded to a Level 4–5 field lookahead — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
